findings.title: Reject malformed BOM/body encodings of reserved storage objects
findings.description: In two isolated committed Git fixtures, a UTF-16LE BOM followed by a UTF-32LE compact-object body, and the corresponding big-endian pair, pass generic availability and the protected-base audit with their payloads absent. json.loads rejects the complete bytes as malformed, while removing the conflicting BOM yields the exact reserved storage object. envelope() trusts the BOM, decodes the body into NUL-interleaved text, then returns None at the ASCII prefilter. read() consequently returns the exact malformed metadata bytes as plain evidence and ignores deliberately wrong expected tested SHA, command and exit zero versus recorded exit one. evidence_exists is True and audit errors are empty. This violates the explicit malformed reserved encoding policy. The actual assertion failure, exact complete input hex, hashes and all outcomes are preserved in verification.json; ordinary standard-encoding absent-payload controls reject correctly.
findings.requested_change: Use recognizable reserved-content bytes to reject malformed or conflicting BOM/body encodings before allowing the opaque fallback. Such a classification must only reject damaged reserved content, never accept replacement/transcoded data as evidence, and must retain byte-preserving opaque historical evidence. Add bounded LE/BE conflicting-BOM negatives covering availability, retrieval, audit and expected execution metadata, then retest and review the new implementation SHA.
